messages:
micah-oncall: :rotating_light: Getting multiple alerts for inference-pool-1 nodes flipping to NotReady, kubelet restarted repeatedly. Started ~16:02 UTC. Seeing GPU resets on some hosts.

infra-bot: [alert] cluster/inference-pool-1: 4 nodes NotReady (kubelet restart count > 2) — auto-tagged severity: high

micah-oncall: Observed on 10.120.48.23, 10.120.48.24, 10.120.49.11. Customer facing error surge: 5xx spike for gen endpoints, latency up. Paging @oncall-sre.

pagerbot: Paging: @micah-oncall (primary) via pager. Incident channel created: #incident-inference-node-flap-1799507777

sara-eng: I'm jumping on logs. Any recent infra deploys?

micah-oncall: No deploys in the last 30m. Autoscaler activity: some scale-outs earlier but nothing abnormal.

kevin-ml: Seen OOM messages in pod logs for runtime container? Can you paste container logs from one crashed replica?

micah-oncall: grabbing container logs from pod inference-abc-7:

```
I0324 16:01:58.123456 1 server.go:123] serving started
E0324 16:02:04.987654 runtime.go:45] runtime error: cuda: GPU reset detected
Killed process 23456 (runtimeserver) total-vm:12g, anon-rss:9g
kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (runtimeserver)\n```

\nmicah-oncall: And node syslog shows repeated kubelet OOM and systemd restarting kubelet: `systemctl restart kubelet` twice in 5m.

opslead: Hypothesis: memory leak or runaway batch jobs causing OOM -> GPU reset -> kubelet crash loop. Could be new batching config?

sara-eng: I'll check recent config pushes to serving runtime. @platform-bot any config changes to batching in last 24h?

platform-bot: No config changes to batching profiles in prod within last 24h. Last change was 2d ago.

micah-oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) cordon + drain the 3 affected nodes then restart kubelet cleanly 2) scale up fallback dedicated pool and shift traffic via routing policy 3) apply temporary pod-level resource limits to reduce mem usage

kevin-ml: For short-term: routing fallback to smaller model variant for high-traffic routes reduces memory and GPU pressure. We should toggle at 10:10 policy to route to model-x-small when node capacity low.

tara-incident: Customer impact: Telemetry shows 12 customers saw >95th latency spikes and 3 customers reported errors. Flagging support to communicate Friday mitigation steps.

micah-oncall: Executing step 1: cordoning node 10.120.48.23 and draining non-critical pods. Running: `kubectl cordon ip-10-120-48-23 && kubectl drain ip-10-120-48-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

infra-bot: Action logged: micah-oncall cordoned ip-10-120-48-23 at 16:08:12 UTC

micah-oncall: Drain succeeded, but evictions slow - some runtime pods stuck terminating (SIGTERM not accepted). Forcing delete on stuck pods with grace 0.

sara-eng: Meanwhile, I'm triggering routing fallback: `redwood-route set --pool inference-pool-1 --fallback dedicated-pool-B --percent 100 --reason "kubelet restarts"`

platform-bot: Routing change applied: all new requests will use dedicated-pool-B as fallback.

micah-oncall: Scaling dedicated-pool-B by +4 GPUs to absorb traffic: `rbctl capacity increase --pool dedicated-pool-B --gpus 4`

infra-bot: Scaling job started (request id: scale-1799507777-01). Estimated ready ~5m.

opslead: After draining, I restarted kubelet on ip-10-120-48-23 via SSH: `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` — kubelet came up clean, node Ready after ~30s.

micah-oncall: Reboot not yet performed. Watching node for relapses.

kevin-ml: We should also look at eviction thresholds — maybe kubelet memory eviction signals too aggressive for runtime's GPU memory usage. Logging a config change ticket.

tara-incident: Support msg draft for affected customers: "We're mitigating an issue affecting inference throughput. We've rerouted traffic to dedicated capacity; engineers are investigating root cause. No model data was lost. Will follow up with timeframe." Approving that.

micah-oncall: Node 10.120.48.24 had same procedure. Cordon/drain, forced pod delete, restart kubelet. That node is back Ready as of 16:22 UTC. 10.120.49.11 still flapping — kernel OOM messages persist, suspect a machine-level process hogging memory.

opslead: Recommend we temporarily taint 10.120.49.11 to prevent scheduling until we can repro/collect full dmesg and get infra to repro on host. `kubectl taint nodes ip-10-120-49-11 critical=true:NoSchedule`

micah-oncall: Done. Collecting dmesg and full journal for infra: `scp` in progress.

infra-bot: Evidence bundle uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-archives/1799507777/evidence.tar.gz

sara-eng: For long-term: open followups: 1) add runtime oomguard to kill only process not kubelet 2) adjust eviction thresholds for GPU nodes 3) add canary routing to detect model memory regressions 4) improve draining playbook for runtime pods.

micah-oncall: Current status: 2/3 nodes recovered, routing fallback active, dedicated capacity absorbing traffic. Latency back to baseline for most customers, support notified.

tara-incident: Elevating to Sev2 incident. Creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem owner.

pagerbot: Handoff: next on-call @sara-eng for 4h. Please update incident doc: https://internal.redwood/infra/incidents/1799507777

sara-eng: Taking over monitoring. Will continue log collection and coordinate infra host repro. Leaving note: do not untaint ip-10-120-49-11 until infra confirms.

opslead: Added tasks to backlog and assigned to infra team for kernel/gpu driver investigation.

micah-oncall: Thx team. Leaving final note: if we see recurrence, perform emergency cluster rollback of recent kernel updates and revert runtime batch config.

tara-incident: Closing live mitigation loop. Will post incident summary and customer impact report within 6h.

sara-eng: Handoff complete — monitoring chat for stale alerts and will update timeline.
